When the Schema Changes

Editing schema.prisma is only the first step — three more bring the running app back in sync with it.

Every topic so far comes together into one checklist for the single most common thing you'll do while building the rest of this API: change what the data looks like.

  1. Edit schema.prisma — add a field, a model, a relation.
  2. npx prisma migrate dev --name <what-changed> — diffs your edit against the database, generates a new migration file, applies it, and regenerates the Prisma Client (the client topic) to match — all in the one command.
  3. Reseed if the data shape changed: npx prisma db seed — only actually needed when the edit affects what the seed script inserts (a new required field, a renamed relation); a change that doesn't touch seeded data can skip this step.
  4. Restart npm run dev if it isn't already running with --watch picking up the change.

Two places worth checking when something doesn't look right after a schema change: npx prisma studio opens a browser-based GUI against your actual database — useful for confirming a change landed the way you expected, without writing a query by hand. And the prisma/migrations/ folder itself is a plain, readable history of every schema change ever applied, in order — worth skimming when you're not sure what state a database is actually in.
